transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-01
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO, Sable AI), Ravi Patel (Lead ML Eng), Marta Silva (Security)

Summary:
Sable is evaluating a migration from OpenAI/Anthropic hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated with a possibility of Private deployment later. Main drivers: cost predictability, latency for low-latency product features, and data residency/security controls. They run a mix of chat and classification/personalization models, currently behind OpenAI + some Anthropic experiments and an internal vLLM/TGI stack for batch workloads. Goal of call: understand Sable's constraints, technical compatibility (vLLM/TGI assets), eval parity requirements, and next steps to run benchmarks and security review.

Topics:
- Current architecture and usage patterns
- Model/ops compatibility (vLLM, TGI, ONNX artifacts)
- Performance and cost targets (p95 latency, token costs)
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
- Pilot scope and success criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya with Redwood, AE on the account. Devon from our SE team is here too. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Lena: Doing well, thanks. Appreciate you squeezing this in, we're on a tight timeline.
[00:15] Maya: Cool, quick agenda. We want to hear about your current stack, biggest pain points, and then Devon will ask a few technical questions about your models and infra so we can propose a pilot.
[00:22] Ravi: Yeah quick intro from us: we run most user-facing features against OpenAI right now, cost is up and latency is kinda spiky for some flows. We've been testing Anthropic for safety models, and for bulk batch embedding jobs we have a vLLM/TGI-based internal runner.
[00:35] Devon: Got it. When you say spiky latency, are we talking p95 or tail events from cold starts?
[00:40] Ravi: Mostly p95 on chat endpoints, occasional 500s during scale-ups. Cold KV cache misses are painful.
[00:46] Devon: OK that matches a lot of other customers. Redwood Dedicated provides pinned GPU pools and we do prefix caching / KV cache to reduce those misses. We also support rolling canaries and automatic fallbacks to smaller models when capacity is tight.
[00:58] Marta: From security perspective we need SOC2, SSO via SAML, bring-your-own-KMS, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Do you support that for Dedicated or only Private?
[01:10] Maya: Good question. Dedicated can be configured with customer-managed keys and we export audit logs; SSO/SAML and RBAC are available. For the highest network isolation and on-prem KMS we recommend Redwood Private, but Dedicated covers most SOC2 and enterprise needs.
[01:25] Lena: Timeline: we want to decide vendor for Dedicated by mid-December and try a pilot in January. Budget is allocated but we need confidence on cost parity versus OpenAI and performance parity.
[01:38] Maya: Understood. On cost, Dedicated is subscription/commit oriented so you get lower per-token unit economics for committed capacity vs hosted. We can run a cost model for your usage patterns.
[01:48] Ravi: Also, we have custom prompts and a few in-house fine-tunes exported as TGI/vLLM artifacts. Will those run natively on Redwood or need conversion?
[02:00] Devon: We support standard model formats; most TGI/vLLM checkpoints can be loaded but there are edge cases. If you have quantized weights or custom kernels, we may need to run a quick compatibility check. We also have a model onboarding team that handles conversions and kernel selection.
[02:18] Ravi: Good. For eval parity, we need exact reproducibility across a set of prompt pairs. Anthropic looked close but not identical in style. How do you recommend we run parity tests?
[02:28] Devon: Typical approach: provide a representative prompt set (we've seen 3-5k prompts for realistic coverage) and we run head-to-head generation and metrics (ROUGE/BLEU and task-specific metrics). We also look at latency distributions and tokenization differences. We'll share a lightweight benchmark script — note that sometimes tokenization differences cause minor divergence.
[02:45] Lena: What's the expected delta that customers accept as parity? 1-2% quality drop or none?
[02:52] Maya: Depends on the use case. For safety or compliance, customers want near-zero regressions. For chat where cost matters, a small drop might be okay if latency/cost tradeoff is favorable. We'll let you define success criteria for the pilot.
[03:05] Ravi: Another concern: we run embeddings for semantic search on large corpora. Are your embedding models exactly the same as OpenAI's? We use dot-product vectors and have tooling expecting a specific dimensionality.
[03:17] Devon: We have curated open embedding models that match common dims (e.g., 1536, 768). If you need exact API compatibility we can map and provide migration guidance. For production-grade throughput we recommend Dedicated with batching and caching.
[03:30] Marta: On the compliance docs, can you share SOC2 reports and your network diagram? Also want to know about data retention and tenant isolation.
[03:38] Maya: Absolutely, I'll share our security pack. Dedicated comes with tenant isolation and configurable retention. For Private deployments you can keep data fully on-prem.
[03:45] Ravi: On the infra side, what integrations do you have with our existing cluster? We use K8s for orchestration internally and sometimes run TGI on our own GPU fleet. Could Redwood Dedicated talk to our metrics/SLO stack?
[03:58] Devon: Yes we have tracing hooks and can forward metrics. For Dedicated, you get network peering options and tracing/traces via our console. We also provide per-route latency and token cost breakdowns.
[04:10] Lena: Cost modeling: we need an estimate for our 2M tokens/day mix of chat (50%), embeddings (30%), and batch classification (20%). Any back-of-envelope?
[04:22] Maya: We'll model it offline but as a quick note Dedicated commit for your footprint usually shows 20-40% unit cost reduction vs pay-as-you-go hosted, depending on utilization and burst profile.
[04:34] Ravi: Does Redwood support zero-downtime rollouts for model versions? We can't have a release that randomly changes hallucination behavior.
[04:40] Devon: Yes rollouts, canaries, A/B tests are supported in the console. You can pin a route to a specific model version and roll gradually. We also support automatic fallback policies to a stable variant if regressions are detected.
[04:52] Marta: Encryption at rest + KMS: is that customer-controlled? Any HSM options?
[04:58] Maya: For Dedicated you can bring your own KMS and we integrate with AWS KMS; for Private we support customer HSMs.
[05:06] Lena: We mentioned vLLM/TGI artifacts — what's a typical friction point when migrating those?
[05:12] Devon: Common friction: custom tokenizer changes, plugins that rely on specific CUDA kernels, and quantized weight formats. Our model onboarding team usually can handle conversions; sometimes we recommend regenerating a model in a supported format.
[05:24] Ravi: For our batch jobs we care about throughput. How does Redwood compare to our current vLLM setup for throughput per GPU?
[05:31] Devon: It depends on model and sequence length, but our serving runtime has kernel selection and continuous batching which can match or exceed vLLM in many cases, especially when you account for smart batching and KV cache reuse. We can benchmark with your workload.
[05:45] Lena: What's the security review timeline? If we need a SOC2 or legal review, how long does that usually take?
[05:52] Maya: We typically provide the security pack within 48 hours. Legal reviews vary but a standard enterprise contract review is usually 2-4 weeks. Dedicated procurement timelines can be faster if you're ok with standard terms.
[06:05] Ravi: Any examples of customers who migrated from OpenAI and kept eval parity?
[06:10] Maya: Yes we've worked with a few mid-market customers — some kept parity by fine-tuning or prompt adjustments, others accepted a model variant with lower latency. We can share anonymized case studies.
[06:22] Lena: About private deployment: would that be in our VPC or do you host an appliance?
[06:27] Devon: Options: private control plane with customer-managed networking (VPC peering) or an on-prem package in an air-gapped mode. For strict data residency you may want the on-prem option.
[06:38] Marta: For the eval parity runs we need logs and diffs. Can you produce token-level diffs and store them?
[06:45] Devon: Yes we can provide token-level traces and store outputs for evaluation. We also have an eval harness to run scoring.
[06:52] Ravi: OK that sounds good. If we do a pilot we want a 2-week head-to-head with our representative prompts and production traffic replay. Is that doable on Dedicated?
[06:59] Maya: That's feasible. Typical pilot: 2-4 weeks, we run parity + perf benchmarks, security review in parallel. We'll scope resources and support.
[07:08] Lena: One small ask: we use a lot of system messages and structured tool-calls. Do you support function/tool calling and structured outputs?
[07:16] Devon: Yes streaming, function/tool calling and structured outputs are supported across our APIs. For Dedicated we mirror the Hosted API behaviors so minimal app changes.
[07:26] Ravi: Any gotchas around tokenization differences causing different token counts and cost mismatches?
[07:31] Devon: Tokenization can differ; we account for that in parity testing. Sometimes minor tokenization delta causes small cost differences but usually not material.
[07:40] Marta: On logging: can we forward audit logs to Splunk?
[07:44] Maya: Yes audit log forwarding is supported. We'll include that in the security pack.
[07:50] Devon: Quick note on vLLM vs Redwood runtime: some customers keep vLLM for heavy batch while using Redwood for latency-sensitive online features — hybrid approach is common.
[08:03] Lena: That might be our path too. We want to avoid a big-bang migration.
[08:08] Maya: Totally sensible. For the pilot we often recommend migrating a single route and running shadow traffic.
[08:15] Ravi: For the benchmarking, can you run on our datasets or do you need sanitized samples?
[08:21] Devon: We can run on your datasets under NDA. If anything sensitive, we can run in your VPC for Dedicated or Private.
[08:30] Lena: Perfect. Budget wise, who manages the Dedicated commit? Is Redwood or our procurement team?
[08:36] Maya: We'll provide purchase options and a quote you can route to procurement. Committed capacity is billed monthly with options for annual discounts.
[08:46] Ravi: Any support SLAs for Dedicated? We need a 24x7 on-call for incidents for production traffic.
[08:52] Maya: Enterprise support is available with defined SLAs. We'll include the SLA tiers in the pricing pack.
[09:00] Marta: One more on encryption: do you do token-level masking or PII redaction out of the box?
[09:06] Devon: We don't do automatic PII masking by default, but we have hooks and recommend pre-processing or our privacy SDK for redaction.
[09:15] Lena: OK wrapping up, what's the immediate next step?
[09:18] Maya: I'll send the pricing pack and security docs. Devon will send the eval parity checklist and a lightweight benchmark script. We want your prompt sets and we'll schedule a SE technical deep dive next week to scope the pilot.
[09:30] Ravi: Sounds good. Can we get the pricing and docs by Friday?
[09:32] Maya: Yes send by Friday.
[09:34] Lena: Thanks all, appreciate it.
[09:36] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.

Recap / Next steps (verbatim):
- Maya to send Dedicated pricing + security pack (SOC2, network diagram, audit log options) by 2026-12-03.
- Devon to share eval parity checklist + lightweight benchmark script by 2026-12-04.
- Sable to upload 3 representative prompt sets and sample responses by 2026-12-06.
- Schedule SE deep dive for technical migration scoping next week.

End of transcript.
